newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick Gold says cash costs rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Barrick Gold says cash costs rise in 1996.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Wednesday its cash operating costs rose US$13 per ounce to US$193 per ounce.
The company, which said it is the lowest-cost major gold producer in the world, said costs should be lower this year.

"With the 40 percent rise in reserves, our annual production will begin to increase quite significantly in 1999. At the same time, our new mines will assist in achieving our objective of remaining the lowest-cost producer in the world," John Carrington, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
Barrick Gold said it is now the second-largest gold producer in the world with 11 producing mines.
At year-end, Barrick's cash position was US$245 million and shareholders' equity rose to US$3.5 billion. Barrick's debt-to-equity ratio is 0.18 to 1.
